The row stays implemented until a W7 mutation run records a symbol-tier kill inside each of the three. Measured by hand in an isolated worktree instead, and stated at that tier: deleting the saveSubscription refusal reds exactly the persistence case on both the memory and the SQLite substrate; encoding an absent attribution as an explicit null reds exactly the codec case; dropping the PackagePin half from the encoded pair reds it as well; and admitting an unattributed Subscription into every withdrawal set reds exactly the membership case. Every kill was an assertion failure rather than a collection error

The store is proved to refuse the changed pair, not to be the only writer of one. WorkspacePersistence.saveSubscription is the single revision path the workspace Actor exposes, and both substrates drive it through the shared test/events/persistence-contract.ts seam, but nothing yet asserts that no other production path appends a subscription record beside it. Closure needs a record-plane check that the subscription namespace has exactly one writer, which is ACQ-OWNER's shape rather than this row's tests
bounds: This rule does not claim the withdrawal sweep. That a withdrawal retires exactly the contributed Subscriptions, and terminates their unadmitted reservations, is C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT's mechanism and evidence; the citation here is WorkspaceRoutingWithdrawal.contributed, the membership query, because the discriminator is what attribution fixity decides.

This rule does not claim §4.2's materialization half. That every record a contribution materializes into carries the same pair is C13-FACET-CONTRIBUTION-ATTRIBUTION, which holds at implemented pending five record kinds this runtime does not materialize; the Subscription is one kind that does exist, and nothing here promotes that atom or stands in for the four that do not.

The durable record and replay prerequisite is implemented: View codec major 2 and ViewDelta documents omit provenance fields on ordinary Views, require both intentDigest and marks on decision Views, reject inconsistent provenance shapes and marks outside the exact body, and preserve decision provenance through memory snapshot restore and file-backed SQLite reopen

The rendering conjunct has no production enforcement point today: Facet Surface.render and ProfileRuntimeEffectsPort.render return generic FacetData, and no production Surface-to-View presenter constructs or validates a View. A codec-only change could preserve marks yet still render marked input as a headline, button label, or unattributed host prose, so it cannot verify this atom

Closing the atom still requires one canonical production presentation path that constructs a decision View from the exact prepared intent, proves every non-host body value is marked with its actual TrustTier, and constrains marked values to data presentation rather than platform voice; no current Surface renderer or ProfileRuntimeEffectsPort performs that composition

testSelectors: test/workspaces/view-replay.test.ts#ViewReplayProtocol [C13-VIEW-DELTA-REPLAY] delegates RFC 6902 and durably replays deltas
test/workspaces/conformance.test.ts#[C13-VIEW-NO-LIVE-STATE] View rejects live non-JSON state

remainingEvidence: The presence discriminator has no encoding. src/workspaces/view.ts#View declares only intentDigest and marks as optional, and ViewCodecV2 decodes an exact field list, so the terminal field §6.3 now defines cannot round-trip. Closure requires the View codec to carry it under §8.3 compatible evolution and requires viewFromDocument to accept the ViewDelta patch that adds it.

Nothing retires a Surface. Withdrawal is planned, which is why C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT is a prerequisite, and no production path emits a final ViewDelta or refuses a later revision. Closure requires one place that both emits the terminal delta and rejects every subsequent revision for that Surface, so the no-revision-after-terminal conjunct is enforced rather than conventional.

EventCursor resume has no liveness branch. ViewDelta replay resolves a cursor without consulting Surface liveness, so a cursor for a retired Surface is today indistinguishable from one for a live Surface. Closure requires resume to return the terminal revision for a retired Surface through the same reader live resume uses, never a second path a client would have to choose between.

The aggregating conjunct has no site. No production Surface composes the surface-backed slot entries §4.2 describes, so dropping a retired child's entry at the next revision cannot be exercised yet; closure requires that composition to read contributor attribution rather than a cached child snapshot.

The behavior test must prove terminality through the public interface — the terminal delta arrives, a further revision for that Surface is refused, and a cursor presented after retirement yields the terminal revision rather than an error — and must detect retirement without holding a live handle, since the rule's cost argument rests on C13-VIEW-NO-LIVE-STATE.
